title: Diagonalizable groups and quotient homomorphisms over commutative rings
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $M$ an additive abelian group. Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Define the $S$-group scheme [def-pc-scheme] $D_R(M)=\operatorname{Spec}R[M]$, where $R[M]$ is the finitely supported group algebra with basis $e_m$, multiplication $e_me_n=e_{m+n}$, unit $e_0$, coproduct $e_m\mapsto e_m\otimes e_m$, counit $e_m\mapsto1$, and antipode $e_m\mapsto e_{-m}$. Here an $S$-group scheme is an $S$-scheme with multiplication, identity section and inverse satisfying the group diagrams. For an additive homomorphism $\alpha:M\to N$ define $D_R(\alpha):D_R(N)\to D_R(M)$ by the Hopf algebra map $e_m\mapsto e_{\alpha(m)}$. In particular the quotient map $M\to M/L$ for an additive subgroup $L$ specifies a canonical morphism $D_R(M/L)\to D_R(M)$. No field or finite-generation hypothesis is required for these constructions.
